rated_messages.input_message: Even though you are stressed, are you willing to sit with this urge until it passes if will help you break this habit?

When smoking, it can feel like your hands are for holding a cigarette, your mouth is for smoking the cigarette, and your chest and lungs need to breathe in the smoke. Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner your body will stop being a trigger for you.
How you would feel later on if you smoked during this social situation? Now think how good you'll feel for resisting!
Instead of smoking, write a quick note to yourself explaining why ditching cigs is important to you. Carry it with you and read it when you feel like lighting up.
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?

Read this rule out loud (if you can): IF someone offers me a cigarette THEN I will say 'no thanks, I don't want one.' Reading out if/then rules has been shown to help people stick with their decisions.
Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.
Ask yourself, "From 0-10, how willing am I to let this urge pass without smoking?" Let it pass to be closer to the things that matter most to you.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
